regions.full_page: I just read your pathetic letter in regard to your little Daughte Lois' eye-trouble. I certainly sympathize with you and your dear Hus- band in this, though coparatively trivial matter. We'll pray, however, and trust that it may turn out to be no more than trivial. It is about twenty years back that a young couple brought their first-born to us at the Monaster of St. Bonaventure, the pupil of whose little eye had been scratched and lost fluid. Their doctor went with them to a specialest in the D. Whitney Bld'g who wanted to remove the eye at once. Then in consternation they came to St. B. and enrollied promising a perpetual enrollment and especially more frequent holy communion. Thank God the eye healed shortly and they never went back to the doctors. So dear Mrs. - and Mr. Bieke - shake off the ex- cessive worry and istead exercise a little con- fidence in God's merciful providence by first promising some even a little sacrifice of some kind in thanksgiving if things go favorable and then, to show your confidence in His goodness, start and thank Him when ever you think of it for what He may see best to do for the little one and for her loving friends.
